correctness.rationale: A disk of radius r<R intersects the polygon circumcircle in an arc of angular size ≤2 arcsin(r/R), by AM–GM on center distance. At radius below R cos(pi/(2n)), the arc cannot contain (n+1)/2 cyclically spaced vertices, so two disks cannot cover all n vertices. At the claimed radius, the polygons clipped by x=0 are convex hulls of original half-side vertices and the two cutpoints (0,±R cos(pi/n)/cos(pi/(2n))). The original vertices have |x|≥R sin(pi/(2n)); the cutpoints obey a strict squared-distance margin R² cos(pi/n) tan²(pi/(2n))>0. Each half lies in its chosen disk by convexity. At equality the majority-run extreme pair forms a diameter of its covering disk, forcing its midpoint center. All odd n≥3, including triangle; no uniqueness of second center claimed.
